title: Odile and the Choir
premise: Rafael Crane fled his hedge-witch mistress to vanish into the Ledger Guild, where clerks record the trade of impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names sold at auction. When he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, he learns the guild has been feeding a parasitic entity that wears King Aldric like a crown, and that his own apprenticeship was the first payment. Guided by Odile, a choir-singer whose voice can unmake bindings, Rafael must choose between exposing the guild that sheltered him and saving a kingdom that never knew his name. In the end he burns the ledgers, frees the king at the cost of Odile's voice, and takes her place as the choir's last note.
about_author: Rosalind Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes in a drafty tower room in the north of England, accompanied by an opinionated cat named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He balances the guild's ledgers on a night of strange trades—a jar of laughter, a widow's shadow—and notices his own handwriting appearing in entries he never made. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine, the comfort of invisibility beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Cataloguing a seized prophecy book from a dead collector, he finds tonight's date circled in ash-brown ink and his own true name beneath it. Emotional beat: dread; the past reaching through paper to claim him.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Mark
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Rafael's POV: his apprenticeship under Mother Yew, the bargain she struck, and the night he ran. Emotional beat: guilt and the realization that running was part of someone else's design.

chapters.title: Odile Sings the Staircase
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A choir-singer employed by the guild to 'settle' volatile trades, she hums a staircase into existence and catches Rafael snooping. Wary alliance forms over stolen wine. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other's masks.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He follows a ledger trail to the guildmaster Vess and witnesses a payment delivered upward—to something behind the throne. Emotional beat: horror; the sheltering institution revealed as a feeding trough.

chapters.title: The King Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Summoned to court to soothe the king's 'melancholy,' she hears two voices inside Aldric—one human, pleading. Emotional beat: compassion curdling into terror as she understands what wears the crown.

chapters.title: Entries in a Dead Hand
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The prophecy book's author turns out to be Mother Yew herself, writing a century ago via a binding she never broke. His name appears on every page after tonight. Emotional beat: vertigo; fate presented as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Choir Beneath the City
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Odile reveals the choir: singers bound to hold the entity's cage-song, dwindling year by year. Rafael realizes the guild's trades have been starving them. Emotional beat: shared purpose kindled in a candlelit crypt.

chapters.title: Vess Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The guildmaster offers him partnership and erasure of his past—if he hands over the prophecy book. Emotional beat: temptation; belonging offered at exactly the price of truth.

chapters.title: Mother Yew's Return
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. His old mistress arrives in the city, alive far too long, demanding her ledger back. She claims she wrote the prophecy to save him. Emotional beat: fury and longing tangled; can a liar's love be trusted?

chapters.title: The Auction of Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the guild's midnight auction, the entity bids for Odile's voice itself. Rafael outbids it with his own name, publicly binding himself to the fight. Emotional beat: sacrifice as declaration; no more hiding.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Cage-Song
chapters.summary: Choir elder Maren's POV. An elderly singer recounts the entity's origin—a king's desperate wish for immortality, paid for with his descendants' futures. Emotional beat: elegiac; history as a debt still accruing interest.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Vess seizes the prophecy book anyway, using a forged entry in Rafael's hand, and arrests Mother Yew. Rafael understands his own writing has been turned against him. Emotional beat: betrayal and self-doubt; his greatest skill weaponized.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The remaining choir attempts the rite early and fails; three singers are unmade. Odile survives but hears the entity learn her melody. Emotional beat: grief and grim resolve; the enemy is adapting.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts Owed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He decodes Mother Yew's cipher: the entity can be unbound only if every debt it holds is simultaneously forgiven or repaid—including his own apprenticeship. Emotional beat: clarity; the arithmetic of salvation.

chapters.title: Prison of Salt and Paper
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He breaks Mother Yew from the guild cells; dying, she forgives his debt with her last breath and tells him the final creditor is the king himself. Emotional beat: reconciliation too late, love expressed as release.

chapters.title: The Crown's Consent
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She reaches the true Aldric buried inside himself and wins his consent to die mortal rather than reign hollow. Emotional beat: tenderness and courage; the hardest yes.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He burns the guild's master ledgers in the counting-house while Vess and the entity's agents hunt him through the flames. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance; debts erased in fire.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. In the throne room, Odile sings the unbinding as the entity tears free of Aldric; her voice shatters mid-verse, and Rafael—whose repaid name makes him a clean instrument—finishes the song. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into harmony.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Silence in the Choir
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The king wakes human and diminished; the choir is freed but voiceless; Odile cannot speak above a whisper. Rafael tends her in the ruined crypt. Emotional beat: tender sorrow; victory measured in what was spent.

chapters.title: What Rafael Signs
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Offered the guildmastership of whatever the Ledger Guild becomes, he instead rewrites its charter: nothing traded that belongs to a person. Emotional beat: hard-won integrity; power declined.

chapters.title: The First Page
chapters.summary: Dual closing POV. Rafael begins a new book—not of debts but of gifts—and teaches Odile to sing again, one cracked note at a time, as spring enters the city. Emotional beat: hope earned; belonging chosen, not bargained.
